A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dual Randomized Smoothing and contain readable main text, equations, 11 figures, six tables, and Appendices A–E. Matching sections and displays supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet evaluations, routing experiments, timing measurements, and ablations in Section 6 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations on both datasets and reports revised numerical results, training costs, and ablation findings.

M1.justification: Section 5.2.1 replaces weighting by the maximum candidate certified radius with a strong weight using the radius at the largest variance predicted over noisy samples. The weak variant already appeared for ImageNet in v1. Zero-radius filtering becomes a general training instruction. The two-stage architecture and certification procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10 and ImageNet for certified image classification and retain the expert-routing scenario. Changes concern training procedures and model configurations within this coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 removes the unfinetuned Multiscale comparator while retaining its finetuned version under revised settings. CIFAR-10 retains the same comparator membership; no new baseline family is introduced.

E3.justification: The main CIFAR-10 training-label construction budget changes from 10,000 to 100 noise samples per radius estimate, a substantial protocol revision. Table 3 also changes Multiscale's ImageNet variance set from {0.25, 0.5, 1.0} to {0.5, 1.0} and removes Carlini's sigma=0.25 configuration. Final certification remains at N=10,000 and alpha=0.001.

E4.justification: Figure 5 replaces the comparison between consistency coefficients 20 and 40 with weak versus strong consistency weighting. Appendix E.4 and Figure 10 remove the 40% and 80% training-subset conditions. The existing analyses of training rounds, candidate variances, sampling budgets, and estimator architectures remain.

E5.justification: Certification confidence levels, their allocation between stages, and Appendix D's confidence-penalty examples remain unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-training seeds, performance error bars, or significance tests. The reduced sampling budget concerns training-label construction.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 6 and multiple experimental curves are revised. Finetuned CIFAR-10 accuracy at radius 0.5 changes from 46.55% to 45.27% under revised training. Table 3 replaces the cited finetuned ImageNet Multiscale results with different-setting results: at radius 2.0, Multiscale now scores 25.2% against Dual RS's unchanged 17.0%, reversing their previous ordering.

T1.justification: The certification assumptions, Theorems 4.1–4.2, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. Section 5.2.1 makes a limited mathematical-definition revision: the strong consistency weight uses the radius at the maximum predicted variance instead of the maximum radius across candidate variances.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list reduce claimed CIFAR-10 relative improvements from 19.2%, 24.2%, and 20.6% to 15.6%, 20.0%, and 15.7%. ImageNet's roughly 1.5-fold advantage becomes 8.6%, 17.1%, and 9.1%. The central certification, adaptive-variance, and routing contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.2.1 expands the explanation of over- and under-regularization risks and why different weights suit CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. Section 6.1 narrows the ImageNet interpretation to small and medium radii and explains Dual RS's fixed computation versus Multiscale's additional certification rounds.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit repository address and redirects the reproducibility statement there. It documents the routing experiment's uniform-weight exception. Table 4 revises CIFAR-10 dataset construction from 48 GPUs × 14.6 hours to one GPU × 6 hours; Appendix C.2 changes total reported training cost from 1517 to 19.5 GPU-hours.

R1.justification: v2 adds Baader et al. (2024) and Mao et al. (2026), and removes the Radford and Dong references associated with the previous ImageNet baseline description. The Balauca entry is a publication/title update of the corresponding work. Positioning against adaptive smoothing and certified routing remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand training explanations, revise experimental descriptions, and shorten the reproducibility statement. v2 adds conference headers and minor wording corrections. The section hierarchy, narrative sequence, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 are reorganized into off-the-shelf and adaptive-finetuning groups. Figure 5's legend changes to weak/strong weights, Figure 10 loses two curves, and several plots are resized. All figure and table identities remain; numerical updates alone are assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the low-budget training option already studied in v1 a concrete main recipe, documents substantially lower training cost, provides a direct code address, and reports headline gains consistent with its revised tables. These improve practical clarity and claim calibration. Benefits are tempered by limited replacement-baseline details and an unexplained default CIFAR-10 discrepancy at radius zero: 68.34% in Table 2 versus 69.34% in Table 6.
